messages.author: 08f3062efe0fd1ca
messages.subject: ordering books en masse
parts:
Dear Rcoholics,

is anyone interested in ordering any R related woodware (books)? Perhaps we could get a discount and lower shipping if we ordered in one batch.

Pretty high on my list are:
Analyzing ecological data
Mixed Effects Models and Extensions in Ecology with R
I'm also waiting for Analyzing Ecological data - Practical Solutions when Things Get Complicated

What books have you been eye balling lately?

If anyone is interested in ordering, please let me know.

Cheers,
Roman

messages.author: 6a305309c154c32d
messages.subject: Re: [Rkoholiki] ordering books en masse
parts:
came across this today, maybe would be of interest, the book is based on
matlab:

http://www.mathworks.com/support/books/book20254.html?s_cid=ACD0210rowBO&s_v1=8284708_1-275XBD

Mathematical Methods in Biology

Written for students in mathematics and biology, this book illustrates
mathematical techniques used in many areas in the biological sciences.
The book begins with an introduction and review of ideas about
biological modeling, calculus, and differential equations. Later
chapters examine standard discrete and continuous models using
difference and differential equations and matrix algebra. Topics covered
include ecological modeling, population dynamics for single species,
statistical inference, and stochastic processes.

-ales

messages.author: 08f3062efe0fd1ca
messages.subject: Re: [Rkoholiki] ordering books en masse
parts:
The book you mentioned is not out yet.

The original plan was to call this book: "Shit happens". But obviously, this is an inappropriate title for a scientific textbook. However, it does represent the type of data sets that are analyzed in this book; zero inflated data with random effects, zero inflated data with spatial correlation, zero inflated data with temporal correlation, data sets with large number of collinear explanatory variables, binary data with spatial correlation, data measured in transects, etc., etc. The book only contains case studies (with R code).
...
We still expect to finish the book by the end of 2011.


According to my sources, this is "the bible" of multivariate statistics:
Using multivariate statistics

On Mon, Feb 22, 2010 at 2:17 PM, Ursa Koce <ursa...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear all,

if someone wants to order books from Springer, I can help with 33% discount.
Just let me know.

Have a good day,
Ursa

2010/2/22 romunov <rom...@gmail.com>

I have received an offer from Lux Libris, a bookstore that deals with scientific literature. They have offered us 15% discount (already calculated into prices). Shipping time is 10-20 days (depends on the book). I have checked some of the prices and they're pretty comparable to those on Amazon.

I will be ordering the following books. If anyone would like to order anything as well, I am willing to lend a hand in handling. Payment is in advance.

Zuur: Mixed effect models and extensions in Ecology with R
Braun: First course in statistical programming with R
Chambers: Software for data analysis: Programming with R



Cheers,
Roman



On Thu, Feb 18, 2010 at 1:50 PM, Maarten de Groot <Maarten...@nib.si> wrote:
I was more hoping for a more R oriented book for multivariate statistics... But I think with this book and a lot of searching for the correct packages you will come far.

lp,

Maarten


romunov wrote:
The book you mentioned is not out yet.

The original plan was to call this book: "Shit happens". But obviously, this is an inappropriate title for a scientific textbook. However, it does represent the type of data sets that are analyzed in this book; zero inflated data with random effects, zero inflated data with spatial correlation, zero inflated data with temporal correlation, data sets with large number of collinear explanatory variables, binary data with spatial correlation, data measured in transects, etc., etc. The book only contains case studies (with R code).
...
We still expect to finish the book by the end of 2011.


According to my sources, this is "the bible" of multivariate statistics:
Using multivariate statistics <http://www.amazon.com/Using-Multivariate-Statistics-Barbara-Tabachnick/dp/0205459382/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&s=books&qid=1266496758&sr=8-1-spell>




On Thu, Feb 18, 2010 at 1:27 PM, Maarten de Groot <Maarten...@nib.si <mailto:Maarten...@nib.si>> wrote:

   I am in for the "Analyzing Ecological data - Practical Solutions
   when things get complicated". The first book you mention however

   Do you know maybe some books on multivariate statistics in
   community data like PCA, adonis, CCA, etc, etc,etc...?

   lp,

   Maarten

   romunov wrote:

       is anyone interested in ordering any R related woodware

       Mixed Effects Models and Extensions in Ecology with R

       I'm also waiting for Analyzing Ecological data - Practical

       What books have you been eye balling lately?
